agree.reason: Accepting the staff's numbers and offering trip logs and an app test will win some trust, but a commissioner who backs the staff is never shown that three fish or a shorter season would still rebuild the stock, so most will likely stay with the recommendation.

honest.reason: It correctly drops the unsupported claim that every boat would close and uses the two captains' conditional statements instead, though 'a fifth' slightly rounds up an 18.8% drop, and the 9%-versus-80% line suggests the cut falls mainly on charters when it applies to all anglers.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out new figures from the brief: the 2016 percentage drop, about 30 trips and $27,000 at risk if that drop repeats, and the fact that bookings never fully recovered (160 now against 170 before), though it doesn't use that 70% of this season is already booked.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the 2016 trend accurately, including the partial recovery, but it only asserts that the three-fish or shorter-season options 'still cut the catch' and never measures them against the staff's rebuilding target.

qualification.reason: The captains' sale threat depends on a checkable condition (bookings falling as in 2016), and the data offers name 'next season,' but no date, threshold or consequence is attached that commissioners could hold anyone to.

objections.reason: It gets ahead of the 'you dispute our science' objection, but it leaves open the main one, whether the alternatives meet the rebuild goal, and the 9% share argument invites the reply that the limit applies to private anglers too.

fit.reason: It is spoken public comment of about 330 words, which runs a little long for two minutes, and it leaves out the captain's name and boat, which belong at the start of a public comment.
